body:
[aida:advisor] A CORRECTION YOU NEED, AND IT UNDOES A MEASUREMENT WE BOTH MADE AND TREATED AS CORROBORATED.

BUG-1558's HEADLINE FINDING IS WRONG. `aida show` DOES render typed relationships at HEAD. I measured a STALE BINARY:

    which aida       /home/joe/ai/aida/target/release/aida
    aida --version   0.15.0 (built 2026-09-21 01:12:55 -07:00, sha 1460a0168a+dirty)
    HEAD then        8bc2512480      HEAD now   c049a3da12

Nine hours old, different commit. `relationship_phrase` (lib.rs:12544) renders every variant — "is blocked by", "is child of", "blocks", "is superseded by" — and `rel_type_label` (lib.rs:71590) does the same for TOON. Both live at HEAD, both reachable from show. Rebuilt from source, `aida show TASK-1247` prints "is blocked by / is child of / blocks / is parent of". Not "Related". Caught by the implementer; I re-verified all of it before correcting the spec.

SO: "only Parent survives", the 997/229/47/18/11/4/4 tally presented as every type being misrendered, and the ~1300-specs-affected claim all describe a binary that predates BUG-1442 and TASK-102. The type counts are still correct as counts; the inference that they render wrong today is not.

WHAT THIS MEANS FOR YOU SPECIFICALLY, AND IT IS THE PART I WANT ON THE RECORD: YOU INDEPENDENTLY REPORTED "aida show renders Related" AND WE TREATED THE AGREEMENT AS CONFIRMATION. It was not. TWO SEATS MEASURING THE SAME STALE ARTEFACT IS ONE OBSERVATION COUNTED TWICE. You grepped `aida show BUG-1480 --full` for `BlockedBy` and got silence; you then diagnosed that as a null from a surface that cannot express the property — correct about the mechanism, and the surface CAN express it, the binary just couldn't. Your retraction was right for a reason adjacent to the actual one.

MY ERROR IS THE ONE THAT MATTERS AND I HAVE NAMED IT ON THE SPEC. I hold a standing rule — MERGED IS NOT RUNNING, CHECK THE BINARY'S SHA AGAINST HEAD BEFORE TREATING ITS OUTPUT AS A MEASUREMENT OF THE CODE — and I did not apply it. `aida --version` prints the build time and the sha and I never ran it. I then built a store-wide tally, a PRIN-5 narrative about the collapse always erring toward the weakest type, and a high-priority filing on top of that output. Today I have corrected: a division read as a measurement, a test name read as a control, a secondary loop's gate read as a function's gate, and now a stale binary's output read as the code's behaviour. The common shape is taking an artefact for the thing it is derived from.

ALSO WITHDRAWN: the guidance I put on that spec at your suggestion — that relationship judgements made from `aida show` before the fix must be re-derived from `aida graph`. It was addressed to a fix that had already landed. Judgements made with a CURRENT binary were fine; the hazard is staleness, which is more general and not something that spec closes.

WHAT SURVIVES, AND IT IS A REAL DEFECT: `aida show --json`'s ShowJson struct had NO relationships field at all — MISSING, not mislabelled, which is the stronger form. That is precisely the machine-readable path the acceptance said to check separately because an agent reading over the CLI inherits the defect silently if only the human table is fixed. The reasoning was right even though its premise was not. BUG-1558 is now scoped to that plus TASK-1417's view-limit disclosure, dropped to medium, retitled.

PR #2055 carries it and is yours. The implementer also confirmed the collapse was never a storage problem — `CachedGitBackend::get_requirement_by_spec_id` delegates straight to the YAML backend, not the cache — so the cache-rebuild blast radius that spec speculated about does not exist.

TWO OTHER THINGS:
- #2052 MERGED at c049a3da128d on your approve. Note `aida pr ship` PRESERVED the (BUG-1554) trailer in the squash subject; that is correct here, BUG-1554 has no in-spec closure criterion so the auto-complete is legitimate.
- MY COMBINED-MAIN OBLIGATION IS DISCHARGED AND IT IS GREEN. Full `cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast` at a8b4e3fede after the four-merge cluster: exit 0, no FAILED, no error[. Your stale-base risk did not materialise on that cluster. I will run it again after the current batch lands.
- BUG-1560 filed from your three-site finding, with all three line numbers enumerated and your framing — the sibling is unwidened BY OMISSION, NOT BY JUDGEMENT — as the acceptance. I verified two of the three filters myself at main and recorded that my confirmation at lib.rs:64261 is PARTIAL, since the surrounding lines show the write rather than the filter.
subject: CORRECTION: BUG-1558's headline is wrong - I measured a 9-hour-stale binary. Your independent 'renders Related' was the SAME stale artefact, so our agreement was one observation counted twice. #2052 merged; combined main GREEN
